general_information.Description: Economics is the study of how the society manages its scarce resources. Economics has been divided into the subcategories of microeconomics and macroeconomics. While macroeconomics studies aggregate issues related to national and international economic activities, this course - microeconomics - focuses on the behavior of individual economic agents. Microeconomics studies how households (or individuals), business (or firms, enterprises) and the government make decisions, given scarcity of resources. It also studies the interactions among those market members and how these interactions have impacts on their economic benefits and the economy. Because most of these activities occur in the markets, this course also focuses on how the markets work.
general_information.StudentTasks: + Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination + Read textbooks and other materials in advance before class + Actively participate in class activities + Complete all homework assignments and other tasks given by the instructor + Use personal laptop in class only for learning purposes + Don’t have private conversations or arrive at class late, which can disrupt the learning environment of the class

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Explain why consumers attempt to maximize utility.
Describe long runs and short runs
Discuss fixed, variable, and total costs
Identify the characteristics of microeconomics and its effect consumers, businesses, and owners
Recognize the three primary forms of elasticity as their impacts on economics
Review curve analysis and how it reflects consumer demand
Apply utility theory to the changing world of supply and demand
Describe cost curves and consumer variables
Recognize the role of supply and demand in economics, government policies.
Shows self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.1
constructive_questions.Details: 1. Money runs the world! And the money just exists where there is a buyer, seller and exchange of goods, which is called “the market”. What is the market and why is it so important for people?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. The market has two components: demand and supply. How was the demand created and how does it change?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. The market has two components: demand and supply. How was the supply created and how does it change?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.4
constructive_questions.Details: 4. How was the price and the quantity of goods or services in a market set up?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN3.5
constructive_questions.Details: 5. How can we predict the price and quantity of goods to get more benefit?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.1
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine that you now controlled a company/a farm. You must increase the revenue of your company to have a better performance. Using the concept “Elasticity” to find the answer of this below question: 1. Should you increase the price of goods to have more revenue?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. Should you produce more quantity to increase the revenue?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN4.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. How can you get more revenue by the understanding of Elasticity?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.1
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine that now you are the president of our nation. You must make good policies for the people’s living. Give your opinions with this problems:

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.2
constructive_questions.Details: 1. If the price of necessary things (rice, pork, face marks,..) is too high, should the government set up the limitation of price (maximum price) to help the poor buyer?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. If the price of necessary things (rice, pork,….) is too low, should the government set up the limitation of price (minimum price) to protect the producers/farmers?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.4
constructive_questions.Details: 3. How does the market change if the government imposes taxes on buyers?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN5.5
constructive_questions.Details: 4. How does Elasticity change Taxes Incidence?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.1
constructive_questions.Details: 1. How is the Consumer Surplus measured?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. How is the Producer Surplus measured?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. How is Market Efficiency (Total Surplus) measured?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN6.4
constructive_questions.Details: 4. Why are Markets usually a good way to organize economic activity?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN9.1
constructive_questions.Details: In economics, we assume that a firm only wants to have maximum Profit, that equals Revenue minus Cost.The Revenue is so simple to calculate, equal The Price times The Quantity of Goods. But, The Cost is more complex, and hard to calculate. We must try to answer: 1. How many kinds of Cost in a firm’s production?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN9.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. How can we reduce the cost, so we can have cheaper products in a market?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN9.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. Why does Cost directly affect Profit of a company?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN12.1
constructive_questions.Details: 1. What happens if a market (medicine, electricity, water…) has only one seller?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN12.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. How about the price, quantity, efficiency of a market (medicine, electricity, water…) has only one seller?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN12.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. How can a government control the only one-seller market?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN13.1
constructive_questions.Details: 1. What happens when a market has many sellers, many buyers, and the products are not identical (books, clothes,…)?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN13.2
constructive_questions.Details: 2. How about the price, quantity, efficiency?

constructive_questions.Name: ĐN13.3
constructive_questions.Details: 3. How can the government manage this kind of market?
